species.real: Red squirrels struggle to digest green acorns while greys manage fine, which gives the greys an edge in oak woods.
species.name: Kindlet

dex.text: Its tail glows like a coal when it is pleased. Buries hazelnuts and forgets most of them, which is how half of Macclesfield Forest got planted.
dex.fact: Red squirrels are now rare in England. Most of Britain's live in Scotland, with others in northern England, on Anglesey, the Isle of Wight and at Formby.

species.real: Red squirrels grow their ear tufts in autumn and lose them in summer, so a tuftless red in July is not an impostor.
species.name: Emberdrey

dex.text: Builds warm nests of twigs high in the pines and keeps them toasty all winter. Other creatures queue to visit.
dex.fact: A squirrel's nest is called a drey. Red squirrels often build several and move between them.

species.real: Pine martens help red squirrels: greys are easier for them to catch, so where martens return, greys decline and reds bounce back.
species.name: Pyredrey

dex.text: Leaps between treetops trailing sparks like a firework. Strictly forbidden in thatched villages.
dex.fact: A red squirrel's bushy tail helps it balance on thin branches, and it wraps it round itself like a blanket when it sleeps.
